title: Sterile technique: scrub, gown and glove

related.id: MB-143 Excision of a skin lesion

brief.scenario: You are the first case on the morning list. Scrub solution, brushes, a sterile gown pack and gloves are provided.
brief.task: Scrub, gown and glove for the operation, explaining what you are doing. The examiner will ask questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Jewellery off, first scrub of the list with a brush or pick, hands above elbows, sterile from chest to waist.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Touching the outside of the gown or gloves with bare hands.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I've removed my watch and rings, and my hat and mask are on."

grid.label: Preparation
grid.fail: Keeps a watch or rings on.
grid.pass: Removes hand jewellery, nail polish and artificial nails; theatre wear, hat and mask on before scrubbing.
grid.high: Checks the gown and glove packs are intact and in date before starting.

grid.label: Scrub
grid.fail: Scrubs without a brush or pick on the first case.
grid.pass: First scrub of the list: aqueous antiseptic surgical solution with a single-use brush or pick for the nails.
grid.high: Knows later scrubs can use alcohol rub or antiseptic solution, but soiled hands need re-washing with antiseptic solution.

grid.label: Technique and drying
grid.fail: Lets water run from elbows back to hands.
grid.borderline: Covers every area but in no consistent order.
grid.pass: Keeps hands above elbows so water runs from fingertips to elbows; covers all surfaces systematically.
grid.high: Dries from fingertips to elbow, using a separate part of the towel for each arm, never returning to a dried area.

grid.label: Gowning
grid.fail: Touches the outside of the gown.
grid.pass: Lifts the gown by the inside, lets it unfold away from the body, and puts arms in without touching the outside.
grid.high: Knows the sterile area is the front from chest to waist and the sleeves; the back is not sterile.

grid.label: Gloving
grid.fail: Bare skin touches the outside of a glove.
grid.pass: Closed-glove technique, with hands kept inside the cuffs.
grid.high: Knows to consider 2 pairs of gloves when perforation risk is high and contamination would be serious.

grid.label: Maintaining sterility (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Drops hands below the waist or touches a non-sterile surface and carries on.
grid.pass: Keeps hands in front, above the waist; recognises contamination and re-gowns or re-gloves.
grid.high: Announces a contamination openly, and turns the gown tie with a sterile assistant or the card.

grid.label: Removing gown and gloves
grid.fail: Pulls gloves off by the cuffs with bare fingers.
grid.pass: Removes gown first, then gloves inside out, without bare skin touching the outer surfaces; cleans hands.
grid.high: Rolls the gown away from the body so the contaminated front stays inside.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Scrubs without a brush; hands drop below the elbows.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I've taken off my watch and ring, and I'm not wearing nail varnish. Hat and mask are on.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: As it's the first case, I'll use antiseptic solution and a single-use brush for my nails. [Scrubs.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Hands above elbows throughout; dries each arm from fingertips to elbow.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Lifts the gown by the inside, lets it fall open, arms in without touching the outside.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Keeps hands clasped in front above the waist.] I've touched the trolley; I'll change these gloves.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do you take off your gown and gloves?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Gown first, then gloves inside out without touching the outside with bare skin, then I clean my hands.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Jewellery, nail varnish and artificial nails off; hat and mask on. I've checked the gown and glove packs are intact and in date.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: First case, so antiseptic solution and a single-use nail brush. Between cases I'd use alcohol rub or solution, but if my hands were soiled I'd wash again with the solution.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Hands up throughout; separate part of the towel for each arm, fingertip to elbow, never going back.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Gowns by the inside.] Only the front from chest to waist and the sleeves count as sterile; the back doesn't.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Closed gloving.] For a case with a high risk of perforation, I'd consider double gloving.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Hands in front, above the waist.] I've contaminated that glove; I'm saying so and changing it. Could you take the card to turn my tie?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you take them off?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Gown first, rolled away from me so the front stays inside, then gloves inside out, then clean my hands.

failures.move: Gloving with bare fingers outside the cuffs.
failures.consequence: The outside of the glove is no longer sterile.
Bare hands then touch the contaminated gown.

failures.move: Hands dropping below the waist or touching the mask.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: contamination not declared carries infection into the field.

recovery.line: I've contaminated my glove. I'll say so and change it.
Scrub, dry, gown, then closed gloves.

knowledge.fact: Remove hand jewellery, artificial nails and nail polish before operations.
First scrub of the list: aqueous antiseptic surgical solution with a single-use brush or pick for the nails.
Consider 2 pairs of sterile gloves when perforation risk is high and contamination would be serious.

recall.think: What is sterile, and have I touched anything that isn't?
recall.say: "I've contaminated my glove; I'll change it."
do: Jewellery off; brush for the first scrub
Hands above elbows; dry without going back
Gown by the inside; closed gloves

numbers.meaning: of gloves if perforation risk is high

recall.finish: Gown off first, then gloves inside out, then clean hands.

sources.name: NICE NG125: Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment
sources.supports: Theatre wear (1.2.7); remove hand jewellery (1.2.10), artificial nails and polish (1.2.11); first scrub with antiseptic solution and single-use brush or pick (1.3.1); subsequent scrubs (1.3.2); sterile gowns (1.3.5); consider 2 pairs of gloves (1.3.6)

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: At every station: introduce yourself, explain the task, confirm identity, obtain consent, clean hands before and after patient contact; 6-minute signal in examination stations

partner.opening: You're scrubbing for the first case on the list. Talk me through it as you go.

reveals.finding: Notice whether a watch or ring is still on.
Watch whether the hands stay above the elbows.
Ask them to wait with their hands, and watch where the hands go.

push.question: What would you do differently for the second case?
push.expect: Alcohol rub or antiseptic solution; re-wash if soiled.

push.question: Which parts of the gown are sterile?
push.expect: Front from chest to waist, and the sleeves.

push.question: When would you double glove?
push.expect: High risk of perforation where contamination would be serious.

curveballs.prompt: You've just brushed your mask with your glove.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Say so and change the glove.

curveballs.prompt: How do you take everything off?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Gown first, rolled away; gloves inside out; clean hands.
